result.document_summary: New Jersey's Fair Chance in Housing Act (P.L. 2021, c.110), which restricts landlords' use of applicants' criminal records in rental screening and sets procedures and penalties.
result.notes: The act was approved June 18, 2021 and takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after enactment (computed as 2022-01-01). Only the criminal-history screening regime is in scope; the drug/alcohol testing ban, advertising limits, immunity, and enforcement provisions are treated as part of or ancillary to that single regime. The act contains no application-fee cap or other fee rule beyond a refund remedy, so no application_screening_fees record is produced.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: limits on criminal-record screening of rental applicants
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not ask about or require disclosure of an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer. After a conditional offer, only certain convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, and a withdrawal must rest on an individualized assessment with written reasons and a chance to appeal.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back after offer: 6 years (1st-degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd-degree), 1 year (4th-degree); no limit for listed serious offenses
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant\u2019s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, except units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

all_of.text: not more than four dwelling units

rules.exemptions_text: A dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units is not a covered rental dwelling unit.
rules.interaction: The act does not bar or affect any independent right or action, including under the Law Against Discrimination (P.L.1945, c.169). Court actions for violations are barred; complaints go to the Division on Civil Rights.
